What I do

Construction and site inspection

I check foundations, formwork, reinforcement, concreting and blockwork against drawings and specifications, and keep daily site records.

Steel and metal works

I check reinforcement bars, structural steel and fabricated metal works for size, condition and workmanship.

Sampling and testing

I take representative samples of concrete, aggregates, steel, blocks and soils, and follow them through to test results.

How I inspect a building, stage by stage

Each stage is checked before the next one covers it. Mistakes are cheapest to fix while they are still visible.

  1. Setting out and excavation

    Positions and levels against the drawings, excavation depth, and the condition of the soil at the bottom.

    The foundation has to sit where it was designed, on suitable ground.

  2. Foundations and substructure

    Blinding, reinforcement, formwork and concrete placement for footings, beams and slabs.

    Errors here are the most expensive to correct later.

  3. Formwork

    Alignment, rigidity, cleanliness and joints before concrete is poured.

    It controls the shape, finish and safety of the pour.

  4. Reinforcement

    Bar size, spacing, cover, laps and condition against the bar schedule and drawings.

    The bars give concrete its tensile strength.

  5. Concreting

    Mix delivery, slump, placing, compaction, cube sampling and curing.

    These decide the strength and durability of the structure.

  6. Blockwork and superstructure

    Block quality, bonding, line and level, mortar and openings.

    They set the quality and alignment of the walls and frames.

Steel, reinforcement and metal works

I look at steel as a material, not only as a bar or a section. Knowing how it is made, heat treated and joined helps me judge whether the steel on site is fit to use.

  • Reinforcement barsSize and grade against mill certificates; rust, scale and bending damage; cutting and bending to the bar schedule. BS 4449, ASTM A615
  • Structural steelSection sizes, condition, connections and alignment of frames, trusses and roof structures.
  • Fabrication and metal worksCutting, bending, fitting and finishing of gates, frames, doors and railings to the drawings.
  • Weld quality, by eyeCracks, undercut, porosity and incomplete fusion, and correct joint preparation. BS EN ISO 5817
  • Corrosion protectionSurface preparation, primer and paint coverage on steel exposed to weather.

The metallurgy behind the checks

  • Strength and ductilityA steel bar must carry load and also bend without cracking. The tensile test shows both.
  • Heat treatmentHeating and cooling change hardness and toughness. Uncontrolled heating on site can weaken steel.
  • WeldingHeat changes the steel around a weld, so preparation and technique matter.
  • CorrosionRust reduces the steel section and its bond with concrete. Coatings and concrete cover prevent it.

Sampling building materials

A test result is only as good as the sample behind it. I take representative samples, label them, protect them until testing, and keep records so every result traces back to the part of the building it came from.

  1. Plan what to sample
  2. Take a representative sample
  3. Label and record it
  4. Cure and protect it
  5. Send it to the laboratory
What I sample and how
MaterialHow it is sampledReference
Fresh concreteSamples taken from the mix at delivery or pour; slump test; cubes cast, labelled and cured.BS EN 12350-1, -2; BS EN 12390-2
AggregatesRepresentative samples of sand and stone from stockpiles for grading and quality tests.BS EN 932-1
Reinforcement steelTest pieces cut from delivered bars for tensile and bend tests, matched to the batch and certificate.ISO 377, ISO 6892-1
Sandcrete blocksBlocks taken at random from each batch for dimension and compressive strength checks.NIS 87
SoilsDisturbed and bulk samples from excavations or borrow pits for classification and strength tests.BS 1377-1, BS 5930

Records I keep

  • Sample ID, date, location in the works, and the batch or delivery it represents.
  • Who took the sample, how it was stored and cured, and when it went to the laboratory.
  • The result, the specification requirement, and the action taken if it failed.

Tests I work with

  • ConcreteSlump, and cube strength at 7 and 28 days.
  • SteelTensile, bend and hardness tests.
  • Aggregates and blocksGrading, and compressive strength of sandcrete blocks.
  • SoilsMoisture content, sieve analysis, Atterberg limits, compaction, CBR and field density.
